## Changes

The commits this session made, oldest first, with the message the agent wrote for each.

### Cap the feature loop's memory with a systemd scope

change `wmmltomzspwx` · [log `891d58bb4741`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/891d58bb4741cfc4975a702efa0d4705b1cfde5a4d7ab4b4fc55958571e0e113.jsonl.gz)

The feature loop ran as part of init.scope, the cgroup WSL shells start in, so a memory-hungry proof could exhaust the machine and take the WSL instance down. feature-loop.sh now re-executes itself in feature-loop.scope with a 4 GB cap (FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX) and no swap. It sets OOMPolicy=continue because the default stops the entire scope on the first kill, which would take claude down with the proof. It refuses to start when less memory than the cap is available or when the scope is still active.

Verified by running the real script with a stub claude on PATH under a 100M cap: the memory hog was killed with status 137, the stub survived, and the loop exited 1 through its usual no-commit path. Also checked refusal for a cap above available memory, an invalid cap and a second concurrent loop, exit 130 on systemctl stop, and that the scope unloads afterwards. A real proof run under the cap was not tested. The separate lib/ work in progress is left out of this commit.

### Limit each JBMC run's memory and report a run that dies as no verdict

change `qwoxmxwmqvqq` · [log `de33e7a7e157`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/a308f9d3-8d8a-42ca-b074-d388818c2418/de33e7a7e157258506656f319c290cff8ca6793d5d3bd32017ce756f83c9451b.jsonl.gz)

One regression proof, ModifiedUtf8#encodeInto, reached 5.7 GB, and nothing stopped it short of the whole machine. Each JBMC run now starts under a 3 GiB address-space limit, set with JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_MEMORY_MB, where 0 turns it off. Its raised oom_score_adj makes the kernel kill JBMC before the agent that launched it. A run that runs out of memory or is killed by a signal now reports unverifiable even if it had already printed a passing line; before, a killed run was not flagged at all.

This does not explain the last WSL crash: that session logged no OOM kills, and the VM was showing clock jumps and CPU stalls before the heavy work. The encodeInto proof now stops after about 16 seconds with 'JBMC ran out of memory', so it has no verdict yet. The README warns against --no-refine-strings, which proved a variant that deliberately differs.

Verified by the agent that wrote it, against the full working copy: 71 tests passed including 3 new ones, clippy was clean, and the encodeInto proof stopped at the limit. The tests were not rerun for this commit, which was split from uncommitted feature work; cargo check --all-targets passed on the split tree. The crosscut and quorum proofs and the feature loop end to end have not run under the limit.

## What changed
- **Memory cap:** the script restarts itself inside `feature-loop.scope`, capped at 4 GB with no swap. To change the cap, set `FEATURE_LOOP_MEMORY_MAX=3G` or similar. `jbmc`, TLC and Gradle all inherit it.
- **Fix to the diagnosis command:** it needs `-p OOMPolicy=continue`. Under the default, one memory kill stopped the whole scope in my test, which would have taken Claude and the current turn down with `jbmc`. Now only the process that ran out of memory dies, and the session sees it fail.
- **Won't start if:**
  - less memory is available than the cap
  - `feature-loop.scope` is still active from another loop or a leftover Gradle daemon; the error message gives the command to clear it
  - `systemd-run` fails, so it never falls back to running uncapped

The README section on the loop now covers this.

### 4. 2026-11-01 21:07 UTC

> Show model name and context usage (current tokens and max tokens) in status line

**Reply:**

The status line now shows the model name and context usage, and no fix was needed. It should look like this:

`user@host:/tmp | Opus 5.5 | 42k/200k`

- **Tested:** I ran the command on a sample payload and got that output, with the original colours and exit 0. With the model and context fields missing, it prints just `user@host:cwd`, also with exit 0.
- **Field check:** I suspected `total_input_tokens` might be a running session total, but [the docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline) say otherwise. It's the tokens currently in the context window from the latest API response, including cache reads and writes, so the number is the right one to show.
- **What you'll see:**
  - Usage shows `0k` until the first API response.
  - Both numbers are rounded to the nearest thousand.
  - Output tokens aren't counted, which matches how the docs calculate `used_percentage`.
  - The docs don't say what the number shows right after `/compact`, so it may be out of date until the next response.

I only tested this on a sample payload built from the docs, not a live session.
